data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 claims the panel 'paradoxically fail[s]' on tasks requiring a counterintuitive mental model because an additive checklist cannot encode non-linear interactions, while the expert overrides it holistically. But SRC_002's own countercondition — that the checklist can be designed with conditional/rule-out logic ('IF A present AND B absent, THEN...') — concedes that explicit, codifiable checklists can encode the exact interaction SRC_002 says they structurally miss. The question's 'explicit checklist' is not stipulated to be linear-additive; SRC_002 silently narrows the stimulus class to additive-only checklists to make the expert win, while conceding that a conditional checklist of the same type (non-expert panel + explicit checklist) can recover the panel's advantage. The argument therefore does not establish that a single expert outperforms a non-expert panel-with-explicit-checklist in general — it only beats a strawman checklist the problem never mandated. The diagnostic evidence SRC_002 offers (presence of non-linear interactions) is not a genuine separator between expert and panel; it is a separator between additive and non-additive checklists.
